editorial:
Imagine being nineteen and trying to keep your life from falling apart while lying to everyone you love. You get to follow a girl who is playing a dangerous game by dating two different guys at the same time. To make things even more stressful, she is stuck attending DUI school, which adds a whole other layer of chaos to her daily routine. The vibe is very raw and honest, feeling more like a peek into a real person's messy life than a polished Hollywood story. It captures that awkward, frantic energy of being a teenager who thinks they can handle everything, even when they clearly cannot.

What really makes this work is the acting, which feels natural and not forced. You will love how the tension builds up as her lies start to tangle together. While the pace is a bit slow in some spots, the payoff is worth it for the laughs and the cringe moments. If you enjoy indie comedies about bad decisions, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, look for the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection.
endingExplained: Everything finally crashes down when the girl's two worlds collide. Her boyfriends find out about each other, and the lies she told to keep them separate blow up in her face. Instead of a perfect happy ending, the movie wraps up by showing her dealing with the fallout of her choices. She has to face the truth and accept that she cannot cheat her way through life or her legal problems.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and cringe comedy.
